title: Split work into atomic commits
when: A working copy has many mixed changes and the user wants them committed as a clean series of focused commits.
inputs: the current changes (git status and diff)
prompt:
Goal: A sequence of commits where each one does one thing, builds and passes tests, and can be reverted alone.
Steps:
1. Read git status and git diff and group the hunks by purpose: formatting, refactor, bug fix, feature, docs, dependencies.
2. Order the groups so each commit stands on the previous one: preparatory refactors first, then the fix or feature, then docs.
3. Stage one group at a time with git add -p (or by file), checking git diff --staged before each commit.
4. Run the tests or the app after each commit when practical, using git stash --keep-index to test only what is staged.
5. Write a focused message per commit; formatting only changes get their own commit.
6. Show the planned list first, then the resulting git log --oneline.
Quality bar:
- No commit mixes reformatting with logic.
- Every commit leaves the project working.
- Messages read like a story of the change.
Pitfalls:
- A final "fix previous commit" commit that breaks atomicity.
- Committing generated or secret files.
- Splitting so finely that commits do not build.
Verify:
- [ ] Each commit has one purpose.
- [ ] Tests pass at the last commit and ideally at each.
- [ ] No unrelated files are included.
- [ ] No placeholder text in messages.
Output: The commit plan (list of commits with files and messages) and the commands used.

examples.input: quebre minhas mudanças em commits menores
examples.output: 3 commits: "Extract price helpers", "Fix tax rounding on discounts", "Document pricing rules"
